instruction: Open a terminal and create a new directory called 'extensions' in the home folder.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened Extension Manager, clicked 'Get more extensions online', navigated to extensions.libreoffice.org, found LanguageTool page, clicked Download. Download was too slow (232MB .oxt) and never completed. Spent remaining turns trying to use corrupt .crdownload file and checking terminal.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Chrome, navigate to extensions.libreoffice.org, search for extensions, interact with LibreOffice menus and Extension Manager dialog, use terminal commands (ls, file)
metadata.failure_analysis: LanguageTool-6.4.oxt download (232MB) was too slow and never completed within 50 turns. Model tried to open incomplete .crdownload file which was corrupt.
metadata.task_rationale: Extracted the terminal capability demonstrated in the later part of trajectory where the model opened terminal and ran commands. Simplified to a basic directory creation task.
metadata.explanation: Task requires opening a terminal and creating a directory. Custom getter runs 'test -d' to check directory existence. Custom metric compares expected vs actual existence.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly checks directory existence at /home/user/extensions using 'test -d' bash command, which is the right approach for verifying directory creation.
Metric correctly handles the 'rule' expected type by directly accessing expected.get('should_exist'), properly receiving the rules dictionary.
Data flow is correct: getter returns {'exists': bool} -> metric compares with expected {'should_exist': true} -> returns 1.0 on match.

Minor coverage gap: instruction says 'open a terminal AND create directory' but evaluator only verifies directory existence, not terminal usage. This is acceptable since directory creation is the verifiable outcome and terminal is just the method.
